title: Revenue is scaling, with a single seasonal spike
insight: Average monthly revenue grew from R$72,733 (first 6 months) to R$231,061 (latest 6 months), +218%. The peak month was Nov 2017 at R$267,775.
why: A one-month spike inflates averages and can hide whether the underlying trend is healthy.
action: Plan inventory, seller capacity and logistics for the peak period at least 8 weeks ahead, and judge growth on rolling 3-month averages rather than single months.

title: Revenue concentrated in a few categories
insight: The top 3 categories (watches_gifts, health_beauty, bed_bath_table) contribute 30.6% of revenue.
why: High concentration raises exposure to demand shocks and seller issues in a few categories.
action: Protect the top categories (availability, delivery SLAs) while testing targeted growth in mid-sized categories with rising trend.

title: Categories losing momentum
insight: Revenue over the last 3 full months versus the prior 3 months fell in: books_general_interest (-51%).
why: Falling categories may signal pricing, availability or demand problems, but the data alone cannot say which.
action: Investigate pricing versus competitors, stock availability and review scores before spending more on promotion. Re-test after one quarter.

title: Very few customers come back
insight: Only 4.0% of 20,332 customers placed a second order; those who did returned after 141 days on average.
why: Acquisition-only growth is expensive. Even small gains in repeat rate compound across a large customer base.
action: Launch a post-purchase journey that offers a second-order incentive around day 20-30 and target categories with natural repurchase (health & beauty, pet, perfumery).

title: Late delivery is strongly linked to bad reviews
insight: Orders that arrive on time or early average 4.39 stars versus 1.76 when 6+ days late. Overall late-delivery rate is about 5.6%.
why: Delivery delay is strongly associated with low ratings, so fixing logistics is likely the fastest lever for better reviews (confirm with an A/B test on delivery estimates).
action: Set seller SLAs and padding on delivery estimates in slow regions, and escalate sellers who breach them repeatedly.

title: A small group of sellers delivers late far more often
insight: The worst 5 sellers (30+ orders) are late on 25% of orders versus a platform average of about 6%.
why: A few poor performers damage the brand for every customer who buys from them.
action: Place high-late-rate sellers on a performance plan, reduce their search ranking until they recover, and share seller scorecards monthly.

title: Large delivery-time gap between regions
insight: North averages 17.8 days to deliver versus 8.2 days in Southeast.
why: Slow regions suffer worse customer experience and higher freight cost, which can suppress demand there.
action: Evaluate regional fulfilment hubs or carrier changes for the slowest region, and investigate whether low sales there come from demand or delivery friction.

title: Cancellations quietly leak revenue
insight: Cancelled and unavailable orders represent R$39,947 of item value, about 1.3% of potential revenue.
why: Unavailable items point to stock-sync problems between sellers and the marketplace.
action: Require sellers to confirm stock at checkout and penalise repeated 'unavailable' cancellations.

title: Credit cards and instalments dominate payments
insight: Credit cards account for 76.8% of payment value; boleto is the main alternative.
why: Instalments let customers afford larger baskets, but boleto customers abandon more often in many marketplaces (not measurable here).
action: Keep instalment options visible on higher-priced items, and test boleto reminders to reduce unpaid orders.

title: Short-term revenue outlook
insight: The best model on hold-out data (Holt damped trend, MAPE 3.1%) projects R$821,923 over the next 3 months.
why: The forecast gives a planning baseline but does not capture holidays or promotions if history is short.
action: Use it as the base case for capacity planning and add judgement for known campaigns; refresh monthly and monitor forecast error.

title: High-value customers are drifting away
insight: 1,204 high-spending customers are 60-180 days past their last order, holding R$477,099 in historical spend.
why: These customers are cheaper to win back than new customers are to acquire.
action: Send personalised win-back offers before day 180 and measure the response against a holdout group.
